checks.invariant: _BodyLimit (api.py:89-148, added at api.py:170) bounds every http-scope body before routing/auth under all framings: Content-Length over cap or non-digit, chunked/no Content-Length, duplicate Content-Length, path/method variants, root_path.
checks.result: Drove the real build() ASGI app (fake docker client, raw ASGI messages) in the sbx sandbox. CL 9 MiB on POST /sandboxes -> 413 with 0 bytes read; CL '+2' -> 413 unread; duplicate CL (999999999999 then 2; dict keeps last) with 10 MiB streamed -> 413 after 9 MiB delivered to the middleware, the app never sees more than 8 MiB; chunked 10 MiB -> 413, same; PUT /sandboxes/x/files -> 405, POST .../files/ -> 307, //sandboxes/x/files -> 404, all under the 8 MiB JSON cap with 0 bytes read; unauthenticated POST /sandboxes/x/files with 10 MiB -> 401 with 0 bytes read (form parsed only after screen_human, api.py:336-340). root_path-prefixed scope paths do not match _UPLOAD_PATH, so they get the smaller 8 MiB cap (fails closed, functional only). After the fake http.disconnect FastAPI handles ClientDisconnect and guarded_send drops later messages; exactly one response.start was sent. A 5000-digit Content-Length makes int() raise ValueError inside _BodyLimit (500 for that request only; in deployment h11 parses Content-Length first). The byte cap holds in every framing.

checks.invariant: Unauthenticated form routes (/login Form, /ui/sandboxes Form) cannot be made to parse or spool more than the cap before auth.
checks.result: POST /login with 10 MiB urlencoded body -> 400 'Field exceeded maximum size of 1024KB' after 2 MiB read (Starlette 1.7.0 FormParser max_part_size/max_fields=1000). Multipart /login with 900 file parts (961 KB) is parsed and spooled into SpooledTemporaryFile objects before the token check (status 200 failed-login page), which is bounded by the 8 MiB cap and max_files=1000 and closed by FastAPI's file_stack. The /ui upload form (templates/sandbox.html:51-53) posts to the same /sandboxes/{sid}/files route, so there is no separate upload parser. Login-failure audit rows (prior agentbox/web.py:unauthenticated-login-failure-audit-growth) are now rate-logged at 5 per 60 s globally with a suppressed count (web.py:89-114) and are removable via the host prune command, so the prior root cause of unbounded attacker-paced rows no longer holds.

checks.invariant: An unauthenticated client's work before principal() is small and does not scale far beyond the body cap (prior agentbox/api.py:preauth-request-body-read-before-principal).
checks.result: Variant not covered by the fix: FastAPI still reads the body and runs json.loads before solve_dependencies, so principal() runs only after decoding. An unauthenticated POST /sandboxes/sb_x/tools/exec with body {"args":{"a":[{},{},...]}} returned 401 with tracemalloc peak 27.4 MB for 1.05 MB and 54.9 MB for 2.10 MB (26x, linear). By extrapolation one request at the 8 MiB default cap allocates about 220 MB of transient Python objects before rejection, plus about 80 ms of event-loop CPU per 2 MiB (about 0.35 s per 8 MiB). The 8 MiB cap was sized for authenticated write_file, but every JSON route gets it before auth. The deploy has no memory limit in docker-compose and no uvicorn limit_concurrency (cli.py:127). Caddy's request_body default is 256MB for all routes (deploy/Caddyfile:7-8), so the proxy does not bound JSON routes.

checks.invariant: Deployment layers in front of the cap.
checks.result: Caddyfile request_body max_size defaults to 256MB for every route (no per-route JSON cap). uvicorn.run (cli.py:127) passes no limit_concurrency, h11_max_incomplete_event_size or body-read timeout, so connections that trickle a body are not timed out. That is uvicorn's general behavior and holds no thread. httptools is not installed in this environment, so h11 0.16 is used, and h11 rejects conflicting duplicate Content-Length values before the app runs.

candidates.title: Unauthenticated JSON bodies are still decoded before principal(); an 8 MiB body that passes the cap becomes about 220 MB of objects
candidates.description: The F1 fix (PR #16) caps every request body before routing, at 8 MiB (AGENTBOX_MAX_BODY) for JSON routes. FastAPI still reads and json.loads the body before it resolves the principal/human_only dependencies. The 8 MiB cap is the same for unauthenticated clients as for authenticated write_file calls. A body of empty objects decodes at about 26x its size, so one unauthenticated request with no token allocates about 220 MB of transient Python objects and about 0.35 s of event-loop CPU before it gets a 401. The fix bounds the work per request but does not tie it to authentication. How many such requests overlap in memory depends on concurrency and threadpool latency. Nothing in the repository bounds either one: there is no uvicorn limit_concurrency and no compose memory limit, and Caddy allows 256MB per request.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Authentication dependencies still run after FastAPI's body-reading and JSON-decoding stage (fastapi routing get_request_handler reads request.body()/request.json() before solve_dependencies). The only pre-auth bound is a byte cap sized for the largest authenticated payload, with no smaller cap for requests that have no credentials and no limit on concurrent pre-auth decodes. Pre-auth memory is therefore bytes x JSON amplification (~26x) x concurrent requests, not the negligible cost of rejecting a missing token.

trace.scope: call_tool route POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/{tool} (body: ToolCall, Depends(principal)); same for create_sandbox api.py:233, restore, decide
trace.description: Unauthenticated client sends a JSON body of up to 8 MiB with no Authorization header.
Only check before routing: the body must be at most max_body_bytes (8 MiB, config.py:65). It is not tied to whether the request has credentials.
Streamed bytes are counted up to the cap and passed to the app.
Runs only after FastAPI has buffered the body and json.loads produced the full object graph (about 26x the body size). Then 401.

evidence.description: _BodyLimit installed with json_max=settings.max_body_bytes for every non-upload route regardless of authentication.
max_body_bytes defaults to 8 MiB (sized so that an escaped 1 MiB write_file fits).

call_tool declares body: ToolCall plus Depends(principal). FastAPI decodes the body before the dependency runs. Local check: 1.05 MB -> 27.4 MB peak, 2.10 MB -> 54.9 MB peak, both 401 (agents/h-bodylimit/artifacts/h.out T7).
uvicorn.run has no limit_concurrency. Concurrent pre-auth decodes are unbounded in source.
Proxy request_body max_size defaults to 256MB for all routes and does not enforce the 8 MiB JSON cap or anything smaller.

blockers: Whether the transient ~220 MB per 8 MiB request turns into control-plane OOM or a stall for the human UI and agents depends on deployed host/container memory and on how many decoded bodies overlap (threadpool latency, concurrency). Both are outside the repository. A safe sandbox check (512 MiB) could only measure single requests at 1-2 MiB.
Overlap of several decoded bodies needs a live uvicorn server with concurrent connections. Starting a server and running concurrent load was outside the hunter sandbox rules.

validation_plan.local: Run agentbox serve on loopback in a disposable container with a fixed memory limit (e.g. 1 GiB) and a dummy human token. Send one unauthenticated POST /sandboxes/sb_x/tools/exec with Content-Type application/json and an 8 MiB body {"args":{"a":[{},{},...]}}. Record the 401 and the peak RSS increase of the uvicorn process (expected about 220 MB). Then send 3-4 such requests concurrently while a sync human route holds threadpool slots, and record peak RSS and whether a human GET /healthz or /ui is delayed. Stop at the first OOM-kill or at peak RSS above half the limit. Regression after the fix: the same requests without credentials get 413 or 401 with no measurable RSS growth.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner checks the memory limit of the agentbox control-plane container or host and whether the TLS proxy enforces a JSON-route body cap smaller than 8 MiB. The bundled Caddyfile allows 256MB on every route.

hardening: Smallest fix for the candidate: in _BodyLimit, apply a small cap (e.g. 64 KiB, enough for /login and htmx forms) when the request has neither an Authorization header nor the session cookie, and keep 8 MiB only for credentialed requests. Better, move token/cookie validation into the middleware for JSON routes so unauthenticated requests are rejected before any body is read. Regression: an unauthenticated 1 MiB JSON body to /sandboxes/x/tools/exec gets 413 or 401 with no body read.

_BodyLimit calls int(length) on any all-digit Content-Length. A value over 4300 digits raises ValueError and returns a 500 (observed via raw ASGI, T6c). Use len(length) > 20 or try/except before int(). In deployment h11 parses Content-Length first, so this is robustness only.

_UPLOAD_PATH fullmatches scope['path'], which includes root_path under a prefix-mounted deployment. Uploads behind a root_path then get the 8 MiB JSON cap. This fails closed (functional only). Match against scope['path'] with root_path removed.

After the fake http.disconnect in the authenticated put_files route, Starlette raises ClientDisconnect out of request.form(). FastAPI does not catch it in an endpoint, so uvicorn logs 'Exception in ASGI application' (log noise, human-only path). Partially spooled temp files are unlinked when garbage collected.

Unauthenticated /login also accepts multipart/form-data and spools up to max_files=1000 file parts (at most 8 MiB in total) into SpooledTemporaryFile before the token check. This is bounded by the cap, but a 64 KiB pre-auth cap would also remove it.

Login-failure logging uses one global 5-per-minute window, so an attacker's failures crowd out per-attempt rows for real failures (they show up only in the suppressed_before count). This is an audit-detail gap, not a growth issue.

uvicorn is run without limit_concurrency and has no request header/body read timeout. A client that trickles a body holds a socket and up to the cap in bytes indefinitely (generic slowloris, no thread held). The bundled Caddy front end is the only place to set read timeouts.
